thread:
Marina (CS): FYI we got a spike from ACME — p99 jumped from ~900ms to ~3.2s around 03:15 UTC. They also pasted a few request/response snippets showing intermittent 401 then a billing 'quota_exceeded' 429. Can eng-sre take a look?
jamie (eng-sre): Looking. Any repro link or request ids?
Marina (CS): They sent a few request ids: req_9a8f, req_9a91, req_9a99. Attached logs show client got 401 then retried, then a 429.
ash (support): I can forward the raw payloads. Quick observation: retries + 429s could amplify traffic into the batcher. If continuous-batcher holds waiting for more tokens, retries might get coalesced into the same batch causing tail blowup.
maya (eng-runtime): Good point. Also recent deploy added a token refresh path that returns 401 for a short window during key rotation. If client retries immediately it can cause bursts.
jamie (eng-sre): Can we confirm timing vs deploy-bot?
deploy-bot: Deploy completed by maya/runtime at 03:10 UTC (rev: runtime-2026-03-17-529) :rocket:
jamie (eng-sre): matches. Let's pull batcher metrics for that host pool (pool: rwd-infer-us-west-1-gpu-a). Looking at batch_hold_time distribution — there's a fat tail starting ~03:12. p95→p99 diverge.
maya (eng-runtime): Paste of batched metrics:```batch_window_ms: avg=12 p50=8 p95=480 p99=2100 batch_size: avg=16 p95=64 p99=128 queued_retries_ratio: 0.32```
ash (support): That queued_retries_ratio number seems high. Client-side 401->retry loop plausible.
jamie (eng-sre): Two hypotheses: 1) token rotation induced 401s -> retries -> microburst -> batcher holdtime grows; 2) billing metering 429s slowed downstream processing so batches backed up. Need logs correlating 401/429 sequence per request id.
Marina (CS): ACME also said they recently changed billing plan — could be borderline on some meter. Tom, any billing anomalies?
tom (billing): I'm seeing a brief spike in meter events at 03:11-03:16 for that org with some 'rate_limit' flags. We sent a soft 429 back to the client at times. Not a full block but jittery.
jamie (eng-sre): Ok combined story: token rotation generated transient 401s, clients retried aggressively, billing sent soft 429s creating slowdowns and backpressure. Continuous batcher kept waiting to fill batches (config patience), which inflated p99.
maya (eng-runtime): Immediate mitigation suggestions: - reduce batcher hold window (grace) from 20ms -> 8ms for this pool - add a short-circuit for retried requests (mark as low-priority or bypass coalescing) - add jittered retry guidance in client SDK docs
jamie (eng-sre): I can push a temporary runtime config patch to lower the hold window on the affected pool. Will also enable a metric tag for retried=true so we can measure effect.
ash (support): Can we get a quick rollback option if it makes throughput degrade?
maya (eng-runtime): Patch baked: change value /pools/rwd-infer-us-west-1-gpu-a/batcher/grace_ms = 8 -> rolled forward to canary hosts. Watchlist: p95/p99, batch_size distribution.
jamie (eng-sre): Initial canary shows p99 down from ~3.2s to ~1.1s and batch_size p99 dropped from 128 -> 40. Good sign.
marina (CS): ACME confirmed improvement in their next few requests, thanks :thumbsup:
tom (billing): I'm also throttling back soft-429 behavior and will follow up with their account manager to avoid unexpected 429s during token rotations.
maya (eng-runtime): Followups: 1) add logic to mark immediately-retried requests (same trace id within 300ms) as non-coalescing 2) add a short-term alert for queued_retries_ratio > 0.2 3) update SDK retry backoff docs to use exponential with jitter (50-500ms).
jamie (eng-sre): I'll open a quick PR for the alert and coordinate rollout. Also adding a one-off eval to replay recorded reqs to verify no regression.
ash (support): Documented repro steps in the internal ticket: steps to reproduce with curl + forced 401 then retry loops. Example:```# simulate token rotation 1) curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer BAD' /v1/generate # 401 2) client retries immediately 3) repeat many times to create microburst```
marina (CS): Customer-facing note: brief incident, mitigated by config tweak and billing throttle adjustments, follow-up with SDK guidance.
jamie (eng-sre): Leaving the canary at reduced grace for 30m, then will either roll cluster-wide or revert based on signals. Current plan: revert to 12ms after we push non-coalesce flag in 24h if no regressions.
maya (eng-runtime): I'll own the non-coalesce change and SDK doc. Tom will coordinate billing. Thanks team.
marina (CS): Good job all, closing loop with ACME and will update ticket later today. :white_check_mark:
